ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(sim): one simulator core for batched envs and sim robots, in-process or served (#4888)

* refactor(transport): share torch-free wire contracts between remote inference and the env server

* feat(sim): run simulators behind one session core, in-process or served by lerobot-env-server

* feat(envs): run every --env.type as a batched env on the session core, in-process or with --env.endpoint

* feat(robots): add SimRobot, a simulated world behind the Robot interface, realtime or lockstep

* build(sim): build simulator images from one Dockerfile.sim and run the benchmark matrix against env servers

* docs(sim): document sim robots and batched envs, each in-process or served

* fix(robots): document that SimRobotConfig needs no calibration

* feat(sim): optional JPEG camera frames for served envs and sim robots

* fix(sim): address PR review: benchmark workflow, record/replay control rate and world reset, RoboCasa mapping, docs

* refactor(robots): serve a sim robot with --robot.env.endpoint, as for a batched env

* feat(sims): declare each sim's robot_type and record it from a sim robot

* fix(ci): run benchmarks without pip on the GPU runner, add missing sim image modules, use the checkpoint's RoboCasa camera mapping

* feat(sims): adding kwargs to make_env

* fix(ci): pin sim image deps, run RoboTwin from its root, skip two tasks that fail on main too

* feat(eval): cap rollouts with --eval.max_episode_steps, 30 in benchmark CI

* fix(sims): port the VLABench instruction (#5022) and typing (#5045) fixes to the moved files

* fix(ci): pin mujoco for metaworld and setuptools for RoboTwin's pkg_resources

* refactor(envs): drop the legacy envs/<sim> aliases, import the native envs from lerobot.sims.native

* fix(ci): check RoboTwin's imports without a GPU at build time, add CUROBO_CUDA_ARCHS for small machines

* refactor(sims): replace the World protocol with a plain SimRobot that autoresets a finished world

* refactor(sim): simplify the simulation foundation (#5109)

* refactor(sim): simplify the simulation foundation on top of #4888

* refactor(sim): follow-ups from the simulation foundation review

- A served environment behaves like a local one before reset: it refuses to
  step or read, rejects call() arguments and starts with the suite's first task.
- Integrations return their environment factories through env_fns(); env_cls
  and the create_<name>_envs aliases are gone.
- validate_checkpoint moves to lerobot.envs.utils and skips the cameras the
  policy's empty_cameras declares, so lerobot.sim holds no policy conventions.
- VectorEnv is renamed LocalVectorEnv, pairing with RemoteVectorEnv.
- Comments say why worker environments are not Gymnasium's AsyncVectorEnv and
  what reusing the describing environment saves.

* docs(sim): state what an env, a sim and the env server are

* feat(sim): name the closest valid key for an unknown LEROBOT_SIM key

* refactor(envs): group the env server options under --env.server

* docs(sim): give the accurate reason _ProcessEnv is not AsyncVectorEnv

* refactor(sim): let the caller start a sim robot's next episode

When an episode ends, the sim robot now stops and ignores actions instead of resetting itself, so strategies are never surprised by a reset. The base strategy and teleoperation start a new episode, the strategy with a fresh policy; replay stops.

Sentry, highlight and DAgger record by time or on demand, not per episode, so they don't support sim robots yet (new supports_sim_robot strategy flag).

* docs(robots): keep hold() where #4888 put it, with clearer comments

* refactor(sim): name the sim robot sim_robot, after its package

* docs(sim): make docstrings and comments short and plain

* fix(eval): build each task's env on first reset instead of in a prefetch thread

* feat(sim): let an integration build its whole batch as one vector env with vector_env_fns

* docs(envhub): test a repo locally through HubEnvConfig instead of removed helpers

* fix(env_server): start a session's presence grace after its first reset

* fix(sim): run LocalVectorEnv under Gymnasium 0.29, which RoboMME's image pins

* fix(env_server): describe a server that finishes starting during the handshake

* test(env_server): skip the slow-start handshake test without the remote extra

* refactor(sim): review follow-ups for the simulation foundation (#5200)

* refactor(env_server): review fixes for the env client, server and vector envs

- Validate the encoding in EnvServerConfig, so a typo fails at parse time
- Document EnvClient's arguments
- Rename instance/session to instance_id/session_id, in the client and in server replies
- Make the client's lock private and drop its unused presence token reference
- Default task_id to the group's first task
- Fail the session if the first result after open is invalid
- Return a StepResult from request()
- Close within the handshake timeout and log a warning instead of raising
- Suggest starting the right server when the deployment is wrong
- Check reset seeds on the server before the simulator runs
- RemoteVectorEnv: same argument order as LocalVectorEnv, reject unknown tasks, accept any seed sequence
- Declare canonical_observations in metadata, so it survives Gymnasium wrappers
- Return render frames as a tuple, as Gymnasium declares

* refactor(env_server): tidy protocol.py

- Name the invalid part (deployment, instance or session) in key errors, as remote inference does
- Keep the constants together so the key functions read as one block
- Plainer docstrings

* refactor(env_server): clarify ServerConfig

- Rename presence_grace_s to initial_presence_timeout_s, as remote inference names it
- Require the deployment, as remote inference does
- Check the resource limits in ServerConfig instead of EnvServer
- Document ServerConfig's fields

* refactor(env_server): tidy _Session and EnvServer

- Rename rgb, fault and seen_client to camera_keys, failure and presence_established
- Pass the transport to _Session and close the presence signals in _Session.close()
- Move the action check next to the seed check, rename encode() to with_jpeg_frames()
- Replace the stop event with a stop() method, as remote inference does
- Log a failed session close instead of stopping the server
- Log unexpected request errors once, in _reply
- Rename count to num_envs, reword two error messages, add docstrings

* refactor(env_server): name each config after the class it sets up

- Rename the client's EnvServerConfig to EnvClientConfig
- Rename the server's ServerConfig to EnvServerConfig
- Import EnvClientConfig from lerobot.envs in tests
- Clarify the server field's comment: a local env may use worker processes
- Drop the envs package docstring and the commented-out gymnasium guard
- List lerobot.sim and lerobot.env_server in pyproject's gymnasium note

* refactor(envs): build EnvHub native batches through the envhub integration

- Move make_hub_envs into envhub as a public make_envs, so factory uses no private helpers
- Import a native batch's env.py once per process, as the shared path does
- Pass make_env_kwargs and provider configs from HubEnvConfig.create_envs
- Bring make_env's docstring to the LeRobot style
- Fix the EnvHub spelling in the LeIsaac docs

* refactor(envs): tidy envs/utils.py after the move to lerobot.sim

- Drop the EnvHub helper and parse_camera_names re-exports, now unused here
- Say when preprocess_observation applies instead of prepare_canonical_observation
- Point integration comments at canonical_observation, which now maps cameras
- Use single backticks in validate_checkpoint's docstring

* refactor(inference): one entry point for robot hold

- List supports_command_hold in the InferenceRobot protocol
- Make configure_position_hold private; callers use configure_hold
- Document supports_command_hold and hold() for hardware integrators

* refactor(policies): import FeatureSpec from lerobot.utils.feature_spec

- Drop the FeatureSpec re-export from policies/chunk.py
- Import it from its new home in policies/__init__.py and the policies that use it

* refactor(robots): simplify SimRobot

- Build the env in __init__; drop the unused reconnect path
- Start the first episode before marking the robot connected
- Inline feature_names at its one caller in rollout
- Create the calibration folder only when a calibration is saved
- Use the observation key constants and single-backtick docstrings

* refactor(robots): lay out SimRobot like the real robots

- Build observation_features from _state_ft and _cameras_ft
- Build get_observation's obs_dict with a camera loop, as SOFollower does
- Type get_observation and send_action with RobotObservation and RobotAction

* refactor(robots): cache SimRobot's feature dicts and document start_episode

* refactor(robots): clarify SimRobotConfig and default to the suite's first task

- Default task_id to the suite's first task, as LocalVectorEnv and RemoteVectorEnv do
- Explain why SimulatedEnvConfig differs for type checkers and draccus
- Call task_id an ID, not an index, and tidy the choices docstring

* refactor(remote_inference): follow the shared transport.protocol layer

- Drop the unused peek_envelope re-export
- List transport.protocol in the README's package table
- Describe hold as the robot's own hold() or position hold
- Type the codec's tensor_converter hook

* fix(rollout): close a resumed dataset that records at another fps

* docs(robots): say a sim robot resets its environment, not its world

* docs(scripts): use single backticks in lerobot_env_server docstrings

* refactor(scripts): parse lerobot-env-server with draccus

- Take --config_path and nested overrides (--sim.task, --zenoh.listen_endpoints) instead of --config/--set/--listen
- Keep a config's sim settings unresolved (SimSettings) until the server fills them from the simulator's conventions
- Require deployment and sim.type, and check endpoints, when the config is parsed
- Restore the previous signal handlers after serving, as the policy server does
- Update the image, compose file, CI script and docs to the new flags

* docs(transport): name the envelope version and the codec's tensor hook

* refactor(env_server): fix each key's request and reply types

* refactor(utils): say what validate_array got and use it for every action check

The local vector env checks actions with validate_array, and the env server
sends its message to the client. Docstrings follow LeRobot style.

* refactor(utils): name the feature in every FeatureSpec error

Feature specs are now built from simulator observations and --sim.state_names,
so a rejection must say which observation failed.

* refactor(sim): fix the Docker install hint and simplify the local vector env

- The missing-simulator hint names a command that works: the sim's server
  YAML, --envhub for EnvHub, and no Docker hint for plain Gymnasium envs.
- StepResult drops the unused sim_time, and task IDs stay ints end to end.
- Rename sim/vector_env.py to local_vector_env.py, after its class, as
  Gymnasium names its vector envs.
- LocalVectorEnv follows RemoteVectorEnv's layout, with each run mode behind
  _reset_envs and _step_envs, a frozen _LastStep per env, and descriptors
  built by keyword.
- _ProcessEnv workers are asked to close together, so a batch shuts down in
  parallel.
- canonical_observation uses LeRobot's key constants and names the feature
  in its image error.
- VLABench records its robot type, and LIBERO drops an overkill quaternion
  check.
- The sim configs and types document their fields, and the PR's docstrings
  use LeRobot style.

* refactor(ci): tidy the benchmark scripts

run_sim_benchmark always passes the episode cap, checks for Docker only when
it runs, and names an unknown benchmark. The scripts' functions are typed, and
the metrics examples use the default LIBERO policy.

* chore(ci): name benchmark jobs and tidy the sim server configs

Matrix jobs are named after their benchmark. The compose health check reads
the required deployment, the server configs say what conventions() fills in,
and the docker README says which images ship torch.

* docs(sim): fix the EnvHub server override and tidy simulation wording

The EnvHub page shows the draccus override for make_env options instead of
the old --set. The benchmark guide names the env server and gives a real
fragile pin, the RoboMME page says its pins stay away from the policy's, and
the simulation page drops "native"/"legacy" and lists the robot type among
the conventions.

* docs(agent-guide): say what the served benchmark path needs

* test(sim): tidy the simulation tests and test the env server in its own process

Add a test running lerobot-env-server in its own process and stopping it with
SIGTERM, as Docker does. Merge overlapping tests, drop the range-seed case, and
run sim robot tests that need no server on a local env, so Fast Tests run them.
Imports move to the top, shared setup becomes helpers and fixtures, and no test
reads private state.

* fix(ci): drop the removed PushT observation size flags from the TDMPC eval target

* test(sim): give an installed LIBERO its default config so importing it doesn't prompt

* test(sim): hide all of LIBERO when testing the missing-simulator hint

* feat(env_server): make the payload limit configurable on the server and the client (#5207)

* feat(envhub): let a repo's env.py define vector_env_fns, so one batched simulator runs a whole batch

* docs(sim): explain the Vulkan loader error in Docker and how CDI mode fixes it

* refactor(env_server): build the payload limits in one place

* docs(sim): fix the EnvHub worker note and the Vulkan tip

* refactor(envs): name the env configs *EnvConfig, apart from the simulators' gym envs

* docs(robotwin): document the served image instead of the legacy native install

* chore(docker): base the policy image on CUDA 13 to match its torch

* chore(docker): base the simulator images on plain Ubuntu

* chore(ci): restore the license headers of the benchmark workflows

* refactor(utils): import the torch helpers from their modules instead of a lazy utils re-export

* feat(sim): let a simulator report its own per-episode numbers (#5253)

* ci(sim): build the benchmark policy image once from Dockerfile.internal, drop Dockerfile.policy and policy_libero.yaml

* fix(sim): listen on the configured endpoint in Docker instead of 0.0.0.0

* refactor(sim): move the sim robot helpers to robots.utils and export package symbols from their __init__

* fix(envs): use LiberoEnvConfig in the XVLA LIBERO processor override

* revert(ci): keep the per-benchmark Dockerfile.policy build for now

* fix(cosmos3): do not flip the canonical LIBERO images a second time (#5246)

* fix(xvla): build the LIBERO input from the canonical observation (#5255)

* Include the environment processors in the checkpoint check (#5247)

* fix(envs): include the environment processors in the checkpoint check

* docs(sim): name Cosmos3 among the policies with environment processors

* add todos

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(robot): yam robot arm with motorbridge (#4855)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(robot): yam robot arm with motorbridge (#4855)

* Add motorbridge-based bimanual YAM follower with gravity feed-forward

* Check python-can using its import name

* Include dataset dependencies in the YAM rollout setup

* Add verified SocketCAN startup helper for YAM

* Wait for asynchronous YAM feedback and protect servo timing during model GC

* docs(yam): include faster gripper tuning in Molmo rollout example

* feat(yam): make faster gripper tuning the library default

* refactor(yam): use shared CAN setup tooling

* refactor(yam): compute gravity compensation with Placo

* feat(yam): add single-arm follower and compose bimanual robot

* fix(yam): register follower configs across CLI commands

* fix(yam): include gravity model asset

* fix(yam): include gravity model in source distribution

* refactor(yam): organize follower and extract position helpers

* refactor(yam): compute gravity torques with shared GravityCompensation

* refactor(yam): extract control step into a pure function

* refactor(yam): move CAN I/O into a _YamBus class

* refactor(yam): move the servo loop into a _Servo class

* refactor(yam): make the connect sequence linear

* refactor(yam): drive bimanual through single-arm public methods

* docs(yam): document control_step and YamFollowerConfig arguments

* fix(yam): harden servo lifecycle and feedback safety

* fix(yam): restore public-index uv.lock and fix docstring order

Restore uv.lock from the main merge: the later relocks resolved against a private mirror and dropped Linux-only markers, which made CI's uv sync --locked fail. Move the freeze_gc entry in YamFollowerConfig's Args block to match its declaration order.

* refactor(yam): align units, names and config with LeRobot arms

* refactor(yam): store gripper calibration in degrees

* refactor(yam): move the robot-independent control loop into mit_arm.py

* feat(yam): damp the arm after a fault and require the motor CAN timeout

* feat(yam): add float mode for moving the arm by hand while idle

* feat(yam): limit gripper force only once blocked, with I2RT's gains

* fix(yam): avoid limit jumps, mixed read-only arms and degree stroke check

* refactor(yam): remove process-wide GC freezing

* fix(yam): rely on firmware watchdog after servo faults

* fix(yam): correct linear gripper gravity model transforms

* refactor(yam): align follower config naming with rebot

* refactor(yam): simplify MIT feedback validation

* docs(yam): add concise follower method docstrings

* fix(yam): reject bimanual actions when either servo is inactive

* docs(yam): simplify setup and safety guidance

* refactor(yam): cleaning

* refactor(yam): replace runtime assertions with explicit errors

* docs(yam): document follower configuration arguments

* refactor(yam): remove read-only mode and safety bypasses

* refactor(yam): load gravity model from URDF bucket

* refactor(yam): use public module facades

* fix(yam): convert gripper feedback to scalar

* refactor(yam): simplify follower config validation

* nit(yam): clarify float mode configuration error

* refactor(yam): remove redundant camera collision check

* fix(yam): calibrate followers during connection

* refactor(yam): use named MIT commands

* docs(yam): clarify MIT motor bus contract

* refactor(yam): name maximum control step

* refactor(yam): clarify internal control API

* refactor(yam): move feedback tolerances into control parameters

* refactor(yam): move motor ordering to the bus

* refactor(yam): simplify the bus feedback checks

- Name the motor IDs and the feedback CAN ID offset
- Let the monitor socket drop error frames, so only feedback frames reach it
- Remove checks that cannot fail: frame types and IDs the socket filters already exclude, the payload motor ID, and a status and finiteness check that repeats the monitor's
- Allow reconnecting after a failed torque-off, since reconnecting turns torque off first
- Share one check that the bus is open

* refactor(yam): remove MIT control checks that cannot fail

- read_joint_state: drop the feedback shape and finiteness check; the bus always returns seven decoded values
- _gravity_feedforward: drop the torque check; the gravity model always returns six finite torques

* refactor(yam): send actions without extra validation

- Clip and submit targets in YamFollower.send_action; a missing target raises KeyError
- Drop the key and finite checks: policy actions are checked centrally before they reach the robot
- BiYamFollower.send_action sends each arm its targets; a fault on either arm still stops both servos
- Remove MitServo.check_healthy, which has no callers left

* refactor(yam): keep the gripper calibration only in the calibration file

- Drop the gripper_closed_deg/gripper_open_deg config fields and their checks
- Build the gripper control settings from the saved calibration, as other robots read theirs
- Stop validating our own calibration file and copying it into the config
- calibrate() keeps the gripper-moved and stroke checks, and reports the measured stroke

* refactor(yam): check the calibration once when opening

- open() uses one _require_params() call instead of a separate is_calibrated check and a parameter rebuild
- Test that opening an uncalibrated arm touches no hardware

* refactor(yam): tidy the follower config

- Rename max_gripper_speed_s to max_gripper_speed: it is in strokes per second
- Make the gripper finger stroke a constant, since it is hardware geometry
- Build the motor feature names in YamFollower and drop motor_feature_names()
- Drop the coulomb_friction sign check
- Document the fields once, in the Args block

* refactor(yam): rename CalibratedGripper to GripperParams

It holds the gripper's gains and limits as well as its calibration, like MitArmParams for the arm.

* refactor(yam): save the calibration like other robots

Drop the atomic-write override of _save_calibration; if atomic saving is wanted, it belongs in the base Robot class for every robot.

* docs(yam): rewrite the YAM page for LeRobot users

Start with what is needed before connecting, give one command per step, add a minimal rollout and an options table, and keep the MolmoAct2 example to its YAM-specific settings.

* docs(model): document GravityCompensation in LeRobot's docstring format

Say that it returns the torques that hold the model against gravity, and write the Args entries in the standard format.

* refactor(yam): drop joint_signs and joint_offsets_deg from the config

YAM's joints read their motors directly; MitArmParams keeps sign and offset support for other arms.

* refactor(yam): drop the adapter serial check, redundant state handling and duplicate tests

- Remove expected_adapter_serial, like the other CAN arms; yam.mdx now suggests a udev rule to give the interfaces fixed names.
- Don't restore the previous calibration when saving fails, like the other robots.
- Clear the shared stop event only in YamFollower.open().
- Remove tests that repeat what other tests already cover, parametrize the stale-feedback and disabled-motor cases, merge the two feature tests, and patch require_package once in an autouse fixture.

* refactor(yam): keep the control settings only on the servo

YamFollower kept a second reference to the servo's MitArmParams; read servo.params instead.

* refactor(yam): use one community name per concept and order methods like other robots

- Name things once, after I2RT and LeRobot: gripper limits, stroke, joint position, initial position, tolerance, disable torque, CAN timeout, servo loop and feedforward.
- Rename the matching helpers: feedback_tolerance, _load_gravity_model, _check_initial_position and MitServo.reset.
- Order YamFollower and BiYamFollower like the Robot base class, with private helpers last.
- Make docstrings and comments plain and short, in LeRobot's docstring format.
- Explain in the MolmoAct2 example how float mode lets the policy start from any position.

* fix(yam): apply the full gravity torque on joint 2

The 10 Nm cap cut joint 2's gravity torque, which reaches 17 Nm with the forearm extended, so the arm sagged in float mode. Use I2RT's 25 Nm bound instead.

* fix(yam): import the YAM robots without the yam extra installed

* feat(yam): support position hold

* doc(yam): update doc

* refactor(yam): connect CAN first, then calibrate and start control on the same connection

- connect() opens the CAN interface first, then calibrates if needed and starts control without reconnecting; calibrate=False still connects only the CAN interface, with torque off.
- BiYamFollower.connect() opens both arms the same way before either is calibrated or enabled.
- open() no longer opens the bus; it connects the cameras, checks the initial position and resets the servo.
- The troubleshooting table lists what a wrong robot.id actually does: connecting asks to calibrate again.

* refactor(yam): give MitServo one set of parameters, passed when it is reset

- MitArmParams holds the loop settings too (control_frequency, feedback_timeout_s, command_timeout_s, idle_mode); the ServoSettings protocol is gone.
- MitServo takes its parameters in reset(state, params) instead of having them assigned from outside.
- YamFollower builds the parameters from its config and gripper calibration when it needs them.

* doc(yam): update doc with molmoact2 lerobot checkpoint

* docs(hub): note that ensure_bucket_file never refreshes a cached file

* refactor(yam): name the gripper force limiter's settings gripper_params

* refactor(yam): make the tracking and float steps return the same thing

* refactor(yam): keep MitServo's loop state private and derive active from its thread

* refactor(yam): move the URDF bucket and cache path to library constants

* refactor(yam): drop unused joint signs and offsets from MitArmParams

* refactor(yam): make connect follow the other arms' calibrate pattern

* refactor(yam): give MitServo its arm and gripper settings when it is built

* refactor(yam): start MitServo from the measured position and use the motor bus method names

* nit

* refactor(yam): use one name per idea in the gripper force limiter

* refactor(yam): name the controller, buses and gripper params like the rest of LeRobot

* doc(yam): nit

* refactor(yam): address review nits on bus and controller naming and connection checks

---------

Co-authored-by: Pepijn <pepijn@huggingface.co>

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(g05): add OpenGalaxea G0.5 policy integration (#4445)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(g05): add OpenGalaxea G0.5 policy integration  (#4445)

* Add the OpenGalaxea G0.5 policy

Native port of G0.5 (Qwen3.5-2B VLA) as policy.type=g05 on Transformers' Qwen3.5
backbone: action expert, flow-matching head, ActionCodec and unified CoT/action
decode, with no OpenGalaxea, Hydra or OmegaConf dependency.

- Codec and tokenizer live in their own modules; the tokenizer and ActionCodec are
  saved as safetensors processor artifacts.
- The relative-action anchor is held while a chunk is in flight.
- The integration code and G0.5 model cards carry the G0.5 Community License.

* Reset the postprocessor when a task change drops the queued actions

In the synchronous rollout, dropping the queued actions on a task change now also
resets the postprocessor, so a stateful step such as the relative-action anchor
starts from the new chunk.

* Fine-tune G0.5 base on new robots from their dataset stats, joints and cameras

- policy.embodiment is a free-text robot name; the released names keep their slot tables.
- Joint slots come from the dataset's joint names (state_slots/action_slots override them),
  and camera_order maps dataset cameras to image slots (null leaves one empty).
- Normalization uses lerobot's normalization_mapping with the dataset's own stats.
- Recipe pipelines load from a Hub repo id, with fewer host syncs.

* Rotate task_aug rephrasings through the training recipe into the G0.5 prompt

The training renderer passed the dataset task as an explicit override, so ${task}
never used task_aug rephrasings for any recipe-based policy. It now passes it as the
fallback (runtime override, then task_aug, then the dataset task).

* Train G0.5 like upstream

- Type-checked under the repository mypy ruleset; flash-linear-attention is recommended.
- Upstream's sample mix of CoT, subtask-as-task and plain samples; the CoT text is cut
  before its Action segment.
- ActionCodec targets leave out body parts the robot does not have (dropout_noop_parts).
- The System 2 chain of thought is selectable (subtask, or bbox and subtask), and
  action codes are masked while it is sampled.
- proprio_dropout_p (default 0.2, upstream's mlp_dropout) drops the state token in training.
- The flow loss repeats the action cache in the targets' row order and detaches the
  VLM KV (knowledge insulation, upstream's default).
- The docs use generic robot and dataset names.

* Configure G0.5 precision with policy.dtype and read recipe_path once

- Precision uses the shared PreTrainedConfig.dtype (bfloat16 or float32) instead of
  model_weights_to_bf16.
- recipe_path is read into the inline recipe when the config is built and then
  cleared, so a saved checkpoint keeps its recipe and the config builds on a base install.

* Check G0.5 joint_signs against the robot's joints after the slots size them

The length check ran in __post_init__ against the checkpoint's raw_state_dim, so
fine-tuning g05_base (14 joints) on a 6-joint arm with 6 joint_signs failed before
the dataset could resize the slots.

* Remove dead G0.5 code

- The ActionCodec's own training objective: lerobot only encodes and decodes with the
  shipped codec.
- The FP32 output-projection cast: the VLM ties its logits to input_proj.
- Inference metadata and batch fields nothing reads, and predict_action_chunk_with_runtime.
- checkpoint_profile and return_continuous_action, config fields that were only validated.
- Unreachable branches: per-sample action encoding, the optional decode mask, and
  attribute fallbacks on objects that always have them.

* Add the G0.5 policy README and refresh the docs

- The README is symlinked from the package (paper link and citation), and G0.5 model
  cards link to the guide.
- Stale references to removed APIs, checkpoint profiles and recipe_path are fixed.

* Simplify G0.5 around the shared lerobot pieces

- Flow times, noise and training inputs come from the shared flow-matching helpers
  (sample_beta, sample_noise, make_flow_matching_inputs; same values). Only the
  pi-convention path the checkpoints use is kept, with upstream's Euler loop: its time
  stays in the model dtype, which the shared euler_integrate does not reproduce in BF16.
- Author samples are built by a processor function, prepare_g05_policy_batch, instead
  of a weightless policy proxy.
- The policy calls its backend directly, and the ActionCodec loads in one place.
- use_language_recipe is read directly, the ActionCodec part/marker list is computed
  once, and the prompt templates share their prefix.

* Return G0.5's System 2 subtask and boxes as the policy prediction

* Retarget lerobot-train's relative_actions_processor override to G0.5's relative step, so relative-action runs resume

* Port G0.5's Qwen3.5 linear attention, vision rotary and position embeddings to transformers 5.22

ns0:entry.ns0:title: perf(datasets): stream-copy videos when deleting episodes (#4498)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
perf(datasets): stream-copy videos when deleting episodes (#4498)

* perf(datasets): stream-copy videos when deleting episodes

delete_episodes re-encoded every kept frame of any video file that mixed kept
and deleted episodes. That work is redundant for datasets written by LeRobot:
DatasetWriter encodes one video per episode and concatenate_video_files joins
them through ffmpeg's concat demuxer in stream-copy mode, so the first frame of
every episode in a packed file starts a closed GOP.

Select and remux the encoded packets instead when every boundary is GOP-aligned.
Alignment is verified rather than assumed, so files packed by other tools still
fall back to the existing re-encode path.

Measured on a 79-episode unitree_g1 dataset (640x480 h264 @ 50fps), dropping 32
episodes: for the three ego_view files 220.6s -> 0.9s, output 364MB -> 306MB,
and the kept frames are now bit-identical to the source instead of a second
lossy generation.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix(datasets): harden stream-copy episode deletion

- Copy codec parameters with add_stream_from_template(opaque=True). Without it, AV1 input (decoded by libdav1d) crashed because no encoder of that name exists, so the fast path raised instead of falling back.
- Only cut at keyframes that are presented before every later packet and after every earlier one. Open-GOP keyframes followed by leading pictures were accepted and produced wrong frames; they now fall back to re-encoding.
- Validate boundaries from packet metadata in a first demux pass and stream the selected packets in a second, so memory no longer scales with the video file size.
- Test stream copy for h264, hevc and libsvtav1, including frame count and timestamp continuity, and add an open-GOP rejection test.

* docs(datasets): shorten stream-copy docstring

* fix(datasets): sort stream-copy frame ranges internally

* style(datasets): format stream-copy range validation

* test(datasets): use video path metadata helper

* docs(tests): clarify packed video fixture behavior

* test(datasets): create packed videos with episode boundaries

* test(datasets): simplify episode encoding fixture changes

* test(datasets): restrict stream-copy regression to h264

* test(datasets): cover stream-copy and reencode deletion paths

* test(datasets): store open-GOP video as test artifact

* refactor(datasets): unify video episode filtering entry point

* fix(datasets): preserve decode timestamps during stream copy

* test(datasets): build the GOP-alignment test dataset directly

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* test(datasets): drop the unused vcodec parameter from the packed-video helper

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* test(datasets): stop asserting which encode path ran in the packed-video test

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* test(datasets): drop unused packed-video changes from test fixtures

The stream-copy tests build their packed dataset through the recording path, so
create_videos no longer needs per-episode encoding.
